overview:
**High fire danger continues today across the Montrose (High Elevation) area, driven by very dry fuels — ERC at 84% and low minimum humidity (22%) tripping one of seven local watchout thresholds.**
- High danger is forecast to persist through August 25, with ERC staying in the mid-80s to high-80s percentile all week.
- Warm, breezy afternoons (mid-70s to near 80°F, NE winds 6–10 mph) will keep fuels stressed, though light rain chances build later in the week.
- No Red Flag Warning is currently posted for the area, and NWS shows no active alerts, but gusts to 30 mph are possible today.
- Gunnison County entered Stage 2 fire restrictions on August 15, banning open burning and campfires countywide. San Miguel County remains under Stage 2 restrictions, and BLM/Forest Service lands across Gunnison, Ouray, Montrose, San Miguel and Delta counties remain under Stage 1.
- The Gold Mountain Fire, 2 miles northeast of Ouray, has burned 39,691 acres and is 87% contained.
- The Elk Fire in Gunnison County's GMUG National Forest is at 7,337 acres and 35% contained per the latest situation report.
